title: Multi-Agent LLMs for Adaptive Acquisition in Bayesian Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2603.28959v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The exploration-exploitation trade-off is central to sequential decision-making and black-box optimization, yet how Large Language Models (LLMs) reason about and manage this trade-off remains poorly understood. Unlike Bayesian Optimization, where exploration and exploitation are explicitly encoded through acquisition functions, LLM-based optimization relies on implicit, prompt-based reasoning over historical evaluations, making search behavior difficult to analyze or control. In this work, we present a metric-level study of LLM-mediated search policy learning, studying how LLMs construct and adapt exploration-exploitation strategies under multiple operational definitions of exploration, including informativeness, diversity, and representativeness. translated_title: 用于贝叶斯优化中自适应采集的多智能体大语言模型
translated_abstract: 探索与利用之间的权衡是序贯决策和黑盒优化的核心问题，然而大语言模型（LLM）如何对这一权衡进行推理和管理仍鲜为人知。与贝叶斯优化通过采集函数显式编码探索与利用不同，基于LLM的优化依赖于对历史评估结果的隐式、基于提示词的推理，这使得搜索行为难以分析或控制。在本工作中，我们对LLM介导的搜索策略学习进行了度量层面的研究，考察了LLM在探索的多种操作性定义（包括信息量、多样性和代表性）下如何构建和调整探索-利用策略。我们证明，在单个提示中同时执行策略选择和候选生成的单智能体LLM方法会出现认知过载，从而导致不稳定的
tldr: 本文通过度量层面的研究揭示单一智能体LLM在同时进行策略选择与候选生成时会因认知过载导致搜索不稳定，并提出多智能体框架以在贝叶斯优化中实现更稳定、可控的探索-利用权衡。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a metric-level study showing that single-agent LLMs suffer from cognitive overload when jointly performing strategy selection and candidate generation, and proposes a multi-agent framework to achieve more stable and controllable exploration-exploitation trade-offs in Bayesian optimization.
